overview.heading: 4 Days Phuket: Phi Phi, Phang Nga Bay, City Tour & FantaSea
body: Phuket has two headline boat trips, and most short packages make you choose between them. This four-day itinerary includes both, on consecutive days, with the arrival day given to sightseeing and the FantaSea show and the final morning left free.

Day two runs south-east to the Phi Phi Islands: Monkey Beach and Tonsai Bay for swimming and snorkelling, a cruise through Phi Phi Leh past the Viking Cave, the calm emerald-turquoise water of Pileh Lagoon and Loh Samah Bay, then Maya Bay itself, before finishing at Khai Island. Day three heads north-east into Phang Nga Bay for the limestone caves of Panak Island, James Bond Island, canoeing at Tham Lod Cave, lunch at the stilt village of Koh Panyee and swimming at Naka Island.

The two days are genuinely different. Phi Phi is open sea, snorkelling and beaches; Phang Nga Bay is sheltered water, towering karsts, caves and a canoe. Doing both is the reason to give Phuket four days rather than three.

highlights.heading: Why This 4 Days Phuket Package Stands Apart

items.title: Maya Bay & the Phi Phi Islands
items.body: The Phi Phi day covers Monkey Beach and Tonsai Bay for swimming and snorkelling, then cruises Phi Phi Leh past the Viking Cave and into Pileh Lagoon — a sheer-sided inlet of calm, emerald-turquoise water — and Loh Samah Bay, before reaching Maya Bay, the beach that made the islands famous. The day finishes at Khai Island for more snorkelling and relaxation.
items.imageAlt: Phi Phi Leh from the air, with Maya Bay and Pileh Lagoon

items.title: James Bond Island & Phang Nga Bay
items.body: The second boat day is a different landscape entirely. The speedboat cruises Panak Island for its limestone cliffs and sea caves — Ice Cream Cave, Keaw Cave or Mangrove Cave, depending on conditions — then lands at James Bond Island, Khao Ping Kan with the offshore stack of Koh Tapu, made internationally famous by the 1974 film The Man with the Golden Gun.
items.imageAlt: Khao Ping Kan and the offshore stack of Koh Tapu, known as James Bond Island

items.title: Phuket FantaSea & the Island's Cultural Side
items.body: The arrival day covers Promthep Cape for its panorama over the Andaman Sea, Wat Chalong — the island's largest and most significant Buddhist temple — and the Sino-Portuguese heritage streets of Phuket Old Town. The evening is spent at Phuket FantaSea, with an international buffet followed by a roughly seventy-minute production combining Thai mythology, illusion, aerial ballet and acrobatics.
items.imageAlt: Sino-Portuguese shophouses and the clock tower in Phuket Old Town

items.title: Canoeing, Koh Panyee & Naka Island
items.body: Within the Phang Nga Bay day, a canoe takes you through Tham Lod Cave at Koh Talu, lunch is served at Koh Panyee — a fishing village built on stilts above the sea, with a famous floating football pitch — and the afternoon finishes with swimming and beach time at Naka Island before the 17:00 return to the pier.
items.imageAlt: The stilt village of Koh Panyee beneath a limestone cliff in Phang Nga Bay

days.title: Arrive Phuket — City Tour & FantaSea Show
days.description: Met at Phuket International Airport for a sightseeing route through the island's scenic, cultural and historical highlights: Promthep Cape for panoramic Andaman Sea views, Wat Chalong for its Buddhist architecture and significance, and Phuket Old Town for its Sino-Portuguese heritage buildings. In the evening, Phuket FantaSea — a buffet dinner followed by the roughly seventy-minute show combining Thai mythology and cultural storytelling with illusion, aerial ballet and acrobatics. Transfer to your hotel in Patong.

days.title: Phi Phi & Khai Island by Speedboat
days.description: 07:30 hotel pickup; 09:30 speedboat departure across the Andaman Sea. Visit Monkey Beach and Tonsai Bay for swimming and snorkelling. Cruise through Phi Phi Leh, taking in the Viking Cave, the calm emerald-turquoise water of Pileh Lagoon and Loh Samah Bay. Continue to the iconic Maya Bay, then on to Khai Island for relaxation and snorkelling. 16:30 return to your hotel.
suggestedActivities: Pileh Lagoon and Loh Samah Bay

days.title: Phang Nga Bay — James Bond Island, Canoeing & Naka Island
days.description: 07:30 hotel pickup; 09:00 speedboat departure into Phang Nga Bay. Cruise Panak Island for Ice Cream Cave, Keaw Cave or Mangrove Cave, depending on conditions. Land at James Bond Island — Khao Ping Kan and Koh Tapu, from the 1974 film The Man with the Golden Gun. Canoe through Tham Lod Cave. 12:00 lunch at the Koh Panyee floating village, with time to see the floating football pitches. Finish at Naka Island for swimming and relaxation. 17:00 return to your hotel.

days.title: Free and Easy — Depart
days.description: Breakfast at the hotel, then Patong at your own pace: Bangla Road, Jungceylon Shopping Mall, the Simon Cabaret show, Freedom Beach, Paradise Beach, spas and massages, Surf House, the Flying Hanuman canopy zipline, Muay Thai at Patong Boxing Stadium or Kathu Waterfall. Private transfer to Phuket International Airport for your departure.

sections.heading: 4 Day Phuket Package from Malaysia — Both Island Trips
sections.body:
The case for four days in Phuket rather than three is simple: it is the length that lets you do both Phi Phi and Phang Nga Bay without giving up the island's cultural sightseeing.

The two boat days are back to back, which sounds heavy but works well in practice — both leave in the morning and are back at the hotel by late afternoon, and the sea conditions in each area are different enough that the days do not blur into one another. The arrival day carries the city tour and FantaSea, and the final morning is free.

sections.heading: Phi Phi and Maya Bay — What to Expect Now
sections.body:
Maya Bay is the beach that made the Phi Phi Islands internationally famous, and it remains the emotional centre of the day trip. The wider Phi Phi Leh route around it is what makes the day: the Viking Cave on the cliff face, Pileh Lagoon's enclosed emerald-turquoise water, and Loh Samah Bay.

Monkey Beach and Tonsai Bay earlier in the day are the snorkelling stops, and Khai Island at the end is the quiet one. Access arrangements at Maya Bay are set by the Thai national park authority and can change; your guide will confirm the day's route on the boat.

faq.heading: Questions About This 4 Days Phuket Package

items.question: Are two full boat days in a row too much?
items.answer: Most travellers find they are not, because the two days are genuinely different — Phi Phi is open sea, snorkelling and beaches, while Phang Nga Bay is sheltered water, limestone caves and canoeing. Both leave in the morning and are back at the hotel by late afternoon, and the final day is free.

items.question: Which nights does the FantaSea show run?
items.answer: Phuket FantaSea performs on Tuesday, Friday and Sunday, and the package includes the show, buffet dinner and transfers on those nights. On Monday, Wednesday and Saturday the Carnival Magic show is included instead.

items.question: Do Malaysians need a visa for Thailand?
items.answer: No. Malaysian passport holders enter Thailand visa-free for tourism under ASEAN reciprocal arrangements. Requirements can change, so confirm the current position before you travel.

items.question: Is this package suitable for families with children?
items.answer: Yes. Both boat days involve swimming and snorkelling from a speedboat with a guide on board, and the canoe stop is paddled for you. Pacing can be adjusted, and the free final morning gives families a slower end to the trip.

items.question: What is not included in the price?
items.answer: International flights and airline taxes, compulsory tour tips of RM39 per person, optional travel insurance, high occupancy and peak season surcharges, and anything not listed under inclusions.
